title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — process, runbooks, postmortems, rotations, game days, and comms
author: Elena Martinez
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standardized on-call and incident response practices: severity definitions, incident lifecycle, runbook templates, postmortem process, on-call rotations and handoffs, game day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), support, and engineering managers.

Scope
-----
- Services covered: hosted API (api-gateway, text-gen, chat-service), serving runtime (model-serving), cache/KV (kv-cache), orchestration/control-plane (control-plane), observability (metrics/ingest), and infra (autoscaler, ingress).
- This document covers production incidents impacting customer-facing availability, latency SLOs, data loss, or security incidents requiring coordinated comms.

Responsibilities
----------------
- Primary on-call: first responder, executes runbooks, triage, mitigations.
- Secondary on-call: backup; takes over if primary is unavailable or when escalation demands extra hands.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates cross-team response for Sev2+/P0 incidents, owns communications and triage decisions until handoff.
- Engineering Manager (EM): ensures staffing and post-incident follow-up.
- Customer Success / Support: external customer notifications using status page templates, coordinates bespoke customer comms when required.
- SRE/Platform: supports infrastructure-level actions and runbooks for infra services.

Incident Severity Definitions and SLOs
------------------------------------
- P0 / Sev1 (Critical): Major outage or data loss affecting >50% of users, or complete service unavailability for a key capability. Target response: page within 1 minute; IC appointed within 5 minutes.
- P1 / Sev2 (High): Significant degradation (latency or errors) affecting a subset of customers or features. Target response: page within 5 minutes; IC within 15 minutes.
- P2 / Sev3 (Medium): Partial loss or non-critical regressions; may be handled by on-call without full IC. Response within 30 minutes.
- P3 / Sev4 (Low): Minor issues, maintenance, or non-urgent defects; handled in sprint.

Key SLO examples (owned by service teams):
- API text-generation: availability 99.9% monthly; p99 latency < 350ms for short requests (<=128 tokens).
- Model-serving: sustained throughput 8k tokens/s per GPU pod under normal load; mean KV cache hit rate > 70%.
- Observability ingest: metrics and traces delivery 99.95% within 1 minute.

Error budget thresholds and automated response
- If monthly error budget usage > 50%, paging to on-call + platform team.
- If > 80% used: initiate rate-limited fallback plan and executive notification.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1. Detection and triage
   - Alert triggers via PagerDuty with playbook link. Pager contains brief: service, symptom, start time, runbook.
   - Primary acknowledges within threshold.
   - Immediate triage: determine scope (blast radius), initial severity, and whether to page IC.
2. Initial mitigation
   - Execute per-service runbook (see Runbook Templates).
   - Apply safe mitigations first: circuit breakers, scale up (autoscaler), temporary routing to fallback variants, feature flags.
3. Escalation and IC appointment
   - For P0/P1, assign IC (usually senior on-call or SRE). IC posts incident channel and status message.
4. Stabilize
   - Focus on restoring customer-facing functionality. Avoid risky long-running changes. Use canary rollouts for fixes.
5. Communication
   - Internal: IC updates #incidents Slack channel and incident doc (timeline + actions).
   - External: Support publishes status page updates using templates below; CSM notifies impacted customers when required.
6. Recovery and verification
   - Confirm SLOs and smoke tests pass. Monitor for regressions for at least 1 hour post-recovery for P0/P1.
7. Post-incident
   - Owner files postmortem within 72 hours. Schedule RCA meeting and remediation tracking.

On-call rotations and handoffs
-----------------------------
- Rotation cadence: 1-week primary rotations, with a 1-week secondary overlap for continuity.
- Handoff process (prior to rotation change):
  1. Outgoing on-call posts Handoff note in #incidents with key ongoing alerts, mitigations, and runbook links.
  2. Confirm contact info, escalation steps, and any sticky tickets.
  3. On-call shadowing: new primary shadows outgoing for the last 24 hours if possible.
- Time off and overrides: use on-call schedule in PagerDuty; EMs must approve long swaps. All swaps recorded in the on-call calendar.

Escalation matrix (example)
- Primary on-call -> Secondary on-call (after 10 minutes unresolved) -> IC (after 15 minutes for P1, 5 minutes for P0) -> SRE Lead -> Eng Director -> CTO.

Runbook templates (per-service)
------------------------------
Each service must have a concise runbook: purpose, trigger conditions, pre-checks, mitigation steps, validation, rollback steps, and contact list. Example runbook snippet for api-gateway: 

Title: api-gateway high-error-rate runbook
Purpose: Restore customer-facing HTTP 5xx errors and identify root cause.
Trigger: rate of 5xx > 3% for 5m or p95 latency > 800ms.
Pre-checks:
- Check PagerDuty alert details and related metrics dashboards.
- Check recent deploys: `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` on deploy orchestrator.
- Confirm traffic pattern: `kubectl top pods -n api` and `curl -sS http://api/health`
Mitigation steps (ordered):
1. Scale up deployment (if CPU/memory pressure): `kubectl scale deploy/api-gateway --replicas=$(expr $(kubectl get deploy api-gateway -n api -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}') + 2) -n api`
2. If new deploy suspected, roll back to last stable revision: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/api-gateway -n api --to-revision=REVIS`
3. Enable circuit breaker or rate limiter for problematic routes via gateway config.
4. If backend model-serving causing errors, redirect low-priority traffic to fallback model variant (model-serving:variant-b) via routing config.
Validation:
- Confirm 5xx < 0.5% and p95 latency < 500ms for 15 minutes.
Rollback: undo changes in reverse order; record timestamps.
Contacts: @primary-oncall, secondary-oncall, svc-owner: api-platform@redwood.com

Runbook best practices
- Keep runbooks short: median runbook length < 500 words.
- Automate verification steps where possible (smoke tests).
- Include CLI snippets and required roles/permissions.
- Mark runbook owner and last-updated date.

Postmortem process and template
------------------------------
- Postmortem required for P0/P1 and recommended for P2s with customer impact.
- Timeline: draft by incident owner within 72 hours; review meeting within 7 days; remediation tasks in tracker within 14 days.
- Postmortem must be blameless, factual, and include corrective actions with owners and due dates.

Postmortem template (fields):
- Title (service + short summary)
- Incident ID and severity
- Date/time window (start/end)
- Summary (one-paragraph)
- Impact (customers affected, quantification)
- Root cause analysis (technical chain)
- Timeline (minute-by-minute for P0/P1)
- Contributing factors
- Corrective actions (owner + due date)
- Preventative measures
- Lessons learned
- Links to runbooks, dashboards, and raw logs

Game days and exercises
-----------------------
- Frequency: quarterly team-level game days and annual company-wide resilience week.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test handoffs, exercise degraded modes (fallback models, rate-limits, partial region outages), test customer comms.
- Example exercise: simulate model-serving GPU pool failure in staging and validate autoscaler, fallback routing, and status communications.
- After each game day: publish a short report, update runbooks, and add remediation tickets where necessary.

Status page and customer communications templates
------------------------------------------------
Use the internal status.redwood.com system for public status. For targeted customer comms, follow Support/CS coordination. Templates below must be used verbatim for timely and consistent messaging.

Status page update cadence:
- Initial: within 30 minutes of incident detection for P0/P1.
- Follow-ups: every 60 minutes for active P0/P1 incidents until mitigated.
- Resolution: final update within 2 hours after recovery (P0/P1) with root cause summary and next steps.

Public status template (initial)
- Title: Service Degradation — [service-name] — Investigating
- Body: We are investigating elevated errors affecting [service-name]. Users may experience increased errors or elevated latency starting at [HH:MM UTC]. Our engineers are actively investigating. We will provide updates every 60 minutes.

Public status template (update)
- Title: Service Degradation — [service-name] — Update
- Body: We have identified a contributing factor and applied mitigations (e.g., scaled pods / routed to fallback). Error rates have decreased from X% to Y%. We continue to monitor while further validation completes.

Public status template (resolved)
- Title: Service Restored — [service-name]
- Body: Service performance has returned to normal. Root cause: short summary. Impact: quantified user impact. Next steps: tracking fixes and timeline for permanent remediation.

Targeted customer email template (short)
Subject: Update: [Service] incident affecting [Customer Name]
Body:
Hi [Customer Name],
We wanted to let you know we are investigating an issue affecting [service] that may have impacted request latency or errors. Our engineers have applied mitigations and are monitoring closely. We will follow up with a summary once we have a root cause and remediation plan.
Thank you for your patience,
Redwood Support

Internal incident comms checklist
- IC posts initial incident note in #incidents with severity, impacted services, initial ETA for update, and runbook link.
- Tag service owners and SRE.
- Update on-call rota and escalation as needed.
- Publish status page updates per cadence.

Metrics and telemetry to collect during incidents
- Error rates (5xx), client-side error distribution, p50/p95/p99 latencies, request rates, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, pod restarts, recent deploy commits and timestamps, and relevant traces sampled at 100% for 30 minutes after recovery (for P0/P1).

After-action and follow-up
------------------------
- Postmortem review meeting: document decisions, agree owner for each corrective action, track in JIRA with SLA for remediation.
- Quarterly review of runbooks and rotation schedule; prune stale playbooks.

Appendix: quick links and contacts
- PagerDuty schedule: https://pagerduty.redwood.com/schedules
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.com/editor
- Slack channels: #incidents, #sre-oncall, #prod-observability
- On-call runbook repo: git@github.com:redwood/runbooks.git

Document maintenance
- Owners: SRE (primary) and platform engineering (secondary).
- Runbooks should include last-updated and owner metadata.
- This playbook reviewed quarterly; next scheduled review: 2026-05-01.

Related pages
- SLOs and error budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Incident postmortem examples: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems-archive
